text: Before making a TLH release, verify local main is up to date with origin/main and has no divergence. A release tag pushed from a local-only commit can publish successfully while main push is rejected, leaving the GitHub Release tag ahead of origin/main until the branches are reconciled.

Gnosis is intentionally mandatory in tlh, not optional. The user explicitly rejected three softer alternatives during this work: (1) warn-and-continue on unsupported platforms instead of hard-failing the installer, (2) keeping /gnosis as a status-only command rather than removing it entirely, (3) keeping 'tlh gnosis' as a wrapper helper for end users. The settings.tlh.gnosis subtree is also scrubbed on next merge rather than respected. TLH_SKIP_GNOSIS_INSTALL=1 exists only as an internal escape for hermetic tests/benchmarks and must not be advertised as a user opt-out. Rationale: tlh works better when agents can consult/update repo-local project memory, so the integration is a baseline assumption, not a toggle. Future contributors may be tempted to reintroduce an opt-out path for unsupported platforms or transient network failures; do not do so without re-litigating with the user.

Human decision: TLH should treat tk as required for architect/product workflows. Install/update should install a managed tk when no valid tk is present, and there should be no user-facing option to opt out of tk ticket integration.

Pi's AuthStorage.set() substitutes the credential object on every OAuth refresh — it does not mutate the existing object in place. Any TLH code that uses a WeakMap keyed on the credential object (or any object-identity-based memo of authStorage.get() results) will silently invalidate on every refresh cycle. The Anthropic OAuth credential shape ({access, refresh, expires}) has no stable non-secret metadata, so identity schemes that depend on accountId / organizationId / tenant_id all fall through to the WeakMap fallback and inherit this behavior. Implication: rate limiters or caches keyed by credential object identity will be reset on every Anthropic refresh and must be paired with a stable token-derived key (e.g. SHA-256 of the access token) to be reliable. tlha-0qw3 added exactly this secondary throttle in extensions/the-last-harness/subscription-usage.mjs.

Disabled TLH primary-agent mode is intended to disable primary-agent persona/tool restrictions and subagent safety validation/gating, but bundled TLH minor subagent model defaults should still apply. The model-default injection should remain opt-out by explicit model on the subagent call, not by /agent disabled.

config/settings.defaults.json sets warnings.anthropicExtraUsage to false. Upstream Pi shows this warning whenever an Anthropic provider is used with an OAuth subscription token (sk-ant-oat...) because, in vanilla Pi, third-party harness usage of a Claude Pro/Max subscription bills as 'extra usage' rather than counting against plan limits.

This premise does not hold under tlh: we bundle @gotgenes/pi-anthropic-auth as a default extension (config/default-extensions.json id 'anthropic-auth'). That extension rewrites the prompts Pi sends so they no longer look like a third-party harness to Anthropic's classifiers (see its constants.js: paragraph removals + the 'Here is some useful information' replacement that otherwise triggers a 400 'out of extra usage'). With that compatibility layer active, OAuth subscription requests are accepted against plan limits, so the warning's framing is misleading for tlh users.

The suppression is coupled to the extension's enablement state so it stops applying once the compatibility layer is gone. scripts/tlh-defaults.mjs commandDisable strips settings.warnings.anthropicExtraUsage when its value is the tlh default (false) and re-adds it on enable when undefined, leaving an explicit user true alone. scripts/merge-settings.mjs prepareDefaults also strips the key from the defaults clone when 'anthropic-auth' is in settings.tlh.disabledDefaultExtensions, so installer reruns cannot resurrect the suppression for opted-out users. If a future change removes either coupling, revisit config/settings.defaults.json — under that scenario the warning would become accurate again for opted-out users.

For the subagent pause shortcut, the user chose simple pause-all behavior over a selection picker: pressing the key should soft-pause all active subagent work, not ask which run to stop. They also accepted pause/resumable semantics for now rather than adding a hard kill path.

Human decision for PR #33: TLH bundles the diegopetrucci/pi-web-access fork as a non-critical default extension for general web research. It keeps upstream tool names (web_search, fetch_content, get_search_content), uses web-scout for general web research, and keeps GitHub/source-history research routed to librarian. Running the upstream pi-web-access extension alongside the TLH fork is unsupported because tool names conflict. The extension must not read or write ~/.pi/; settings and cache stay under the isolated TLH profile via PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR.

Human decision for PR #33: TLH must not automatically migrate ~/.pi/web-search.json or persist EXA API keys during settings merges. Users may manually copy an existing key into the isolated pi-web-access settings file. EXA key precedence is explicit isolated extension settings, then EXA_API_KEY, then the zero-config Exa MCP fallback.

TLH intentionally pins the isolated profile setting lastChangelogVersion to 9999.0.0 so upstream Pi automatic changelog/update notices stay hidden in tlh. This uses a static sentinel instead of checking the installed Pi version on every launch because pi --version measured as noticeable startup overhead (~0.3-0.5s). The behavior is not user-configurable: tlh should keep startup quiet while still leaving manual upstream /changelog available and providing /tlh-changelog for TLH release notes. This applies only to the isolated TLH profile, never normal ~/.pi/agent.

TLH intentionally keeps package.json exporting ./skills even when the directory has no user-facing skills today, so future packaged skills can be added without changing the package resource shape. Contributor-only workflow skills such as harness-setup should live under repo-local .pi/skills instead so installed tlh users do not see them.

User chose that diegopetrucci/pi-subagents main should carry the TLH fork patches instead of leaving prior TLH work reachable only through pin tags. On 2026-05-24, main/v0.26.0 was merged with tlh-v0.25.0-3 and tagged tlh-v0.26.0-1; future TLH pi-subagents pins should prefer tags reachable from the fork main unless there is an explicit reason to diverge.

The fork-tag and pin-selection workflow above is historical and superseded by bdysgr. Subagents now ship as first-party root-package code in extensions/subagents, so do not create a standalone subagent tag or pin from this entry. The original body remains verbatim as a dated human decision; this note makes no claim about current repository or tag hosting state.

For TLH bundled extension maintenance/power-user commands, the user confirmed autocomplete hiding is sufficient: commands such as /fff-health, /fff-rescan, /fff-mode, and /intercom do not need to be blocked from manual execution. Avoid forking extensions solely to prevent knowledgeable users from typing those commands directly.
uninstall.sh deliberately has no confirmation prompt

AGENT_DIR is the unit of TLH ownership; PROFILE_ROOT (dirname AGENT_DIR) may contain unrelated user data. Uninstall must only rm -rf AGENT_DIR, then best-effort rmdir PROFILE_ROOT non-recursively. Earlier code recursed into PROFILE_ROOT and could destroy sibling data on custom --agent-dir.

Human decision: TLH is a batteries-included install experience. For required installer dependencies and runtime pieces, prefer automatically installing the managed/default dependency and hard-failing with an actionable error if that cannot be done, rather than adding defensive opt-out paths that let users create incomplete installs. In particular, required upstream Pi runtime handling should install Pi when missing and fail if installation or version validation cannot satisfy TLH's minimum requirement; optional flags like --no-pi-install are not aligned with this policy.

User chose that diegopetrucci/pi-intercom should not keep long-lived TLH branches for profile/fork patches. On 2026-05-30 the TLH intercom lineage was moved onto fork main, tagged tlh-v0.6.0-3, and the remote tlh-profile-dir branch was deleted. Future TLH pi-intercom pins should prefer tags reachable from fork main unless there is an explicit reason to diverge.

Human decision on 2026-06-04: when TLH needs a pi-subagents fork fix for bundled pinning, open a PR in diegopetrucci/pi-subagents and wait for review/merge before creating the reachable TLH tag and bumping config/default-extensions.json. Do not tag-and-pin directly before review unless the user explicitly overrides this flow.

The general PR-first rule for TLH dependencies that are still external remains recorded in pjvejy; do not infer a current subagent release workflow from this dated body.

When context-cap was moved from a bundled default extension into TLH core (branch 'context-cap', 2026-06-03), the human explicitly chose a force-uninstall, non-conservative migration over the usual conservative pattern: (1) npm:@diegopetrucci/pi-context-cap is unconditionally removed from existing isolated profiles on every merge, and (2) any prior 'context-cap' entry in tlh.disabledDefaultExtensions is silently pruned without translation to the new tlh.contextCap.disabled setting. Reasoning the human gave: users who previously opted out can re-opt-out via /toggle-context-cap or tlh.contextCap.disabled: true; the cap is now the TLH default, and dragging legacy opt-outs forward would add migration surface for negligible UX benefit. If a future similar move comes up (another bundled extension becoming core), the prior art here intentionally rejects opt-out translation.

The tlh wrapper at ~/.local/bin/tlh used to call `pi --version` on every launch to enforce MIN_PI_VERSION and to fall back from a stale PATH-front pi to ~/.local/bin/pi. That probe cost ~0.5s per launch.

On 2026-06-04 we replaced the per-launch probe with a pinned absolute pi path baked into the rendered wrapper at install/update time (`scripts/tlh-wrapper.mjs` --pi-cmd, plumbed from `installPiIfNeeded` in `scripts/tlh-install.mjs`). The fast path skips the version probe entirely; the previous resolver remains as a fallback when the pin is missing or non-executable. The update/defaults/tickets subcommand branches still use the resolver because the update child re-runs the bash installer which itself probes for pi.

RECURRENCE (2026-06-22): the per-launch `pi --version` probe crept back into the rendered wrapper as part of the private-runtime migration (gnosis hczfaj) — an unconditional probe + tlh_pi_version_meets_minimum hard-floor + pinned-version-mismatch soft-warn ran on EVERY launch, costing ~0.37s measured. It was removed again, restoring the direct-exec fast path (only the empty-default_pi_cmd and `[[ -x default_pi_cmd ]]` guards remain before exec). Lesson: this probe keeps getting re-added by well-meaning runtime-validation changes. Do NOT re-add per-launch version validation; the pinned absolute private runtime makes it redundant and enforcement already lives at install/update time in tlh-install.mjs (assertSupportedPiVersion + installPiIfNeeded).

Alternatives considered and rejected:

1. mtime-based cache (re-validate only when pi binary's mtime changes). Adds a stat per launch and a cache invalidation surface for marginal benefit over pinning.

2. Caching the full pi --version output. Same complexity, same trust problem.

3. Sourced resolved-state file under the isolated agent dir (vs. baking into the wrapper). The agent dir is under more lenient write surface; sourcing arbitrary shell from there is a slightly worse posture than a literal in ~/.local/bin/tlh. Reach for this only if more machine-resolved values accumulate.

Accepted trade-off: minimum-pi-version enforcement moves from per-launch to install/update time. If a user replaces ~/.local/bin/pi in place with an unsupported version (e.g. downgrade against the same symlink), the wrapper will silently exec it. README and CHANGELOG state this explicitly; `tlh update` is the documented recourse.

The per-user-fallback branch in installPiIfNeeded must pin piBin directly, NOT a fresh `command -v pi` lookup at the function's return point — at that point PATH may still resolve to the stale earlier-PATH pi. There is a regression test ("per-user-fallback branch bakes piBin as default_pi_cmd even when stale pi is earlier on PATH") guarding this; do not weaken or delete it.

Related: gnosis entry gbeuvt records the same per-launch `pi --version` overhead being rejected earlier for the lastChangelogVersion check.

The user wanted TLH to suggest/discover commands, features, and similar affordances, noting Claude Code and other harnesses do this. During implementation they explicitly chose a quiet hand-curated startup tip: show at most one random tip per TLH process launch, with no hourly rotation, timers, popups, settings writes, or LLM-generated suggestions. Preserve existing autocomplete-hiding behavior for power-user/internal commands unless explicitly changed. Update 2026-07-11: the human confirmed the discoverability request is fulfilled by launch tips; do not re-propose feature/command discoverability as a TLH improvement.

Human decision from 2026-06-05: PR #112's run-tests-last workflow guidance should be opt-in only. Keep the behavior gated behind the TLH /experimental feature run-tests-last; do not merge or apply those architect/developer prompt changes unconditionally.

Human workflow decision: every TLH pull request description should include an 'Install this branch' command at the bottom for the PR branch. Use the branch's raw install.sh URL and pass the matching --ref plus --track ref, e.g. curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diegopetrucci/the-last-harness/<branch>/install.sh | bash -s -- --ref <branch> --track ref.

2026-06-10 librarian SIGTERM investigation: end-user report on TLH v0.16.0 / pi-subagents tlh-v0.26.0-3 showed child runs failing with exit 143 but artifacts containing only partial assistant preamble. Current TLH v0.19.0 / pi-subagents tlh-v0.26.0-5 did not reproduce, and no pi-subagents control watchdog kill path was found. The accepted direction is an observability fix in pi-subagents: synthesize factual diagnostics for non-zero child exits with empty stderr, avoid overclaiming the SIGTERM sender, and surface the diagnostic in tool responses, intercom/status/result metadata, and human-readable artifacts/logs while preserving partial output.

The dated non-reproduction and observability principle remain evidence. If current failures show the same diagnostic gap, selectively adopt the still-valid idea directly in first-party extensions/subagents after reproducing it against the current runtime; do not create a fork pin, release, or sync task from the old wording.

Human decision: TLH bundled OpenAI model defaults should be subscription-only. Do not add regular OpenAI API provider candidates (openai/...) back to bundled primary/subagent tlhOpenaiModels as automatic fallbacks; use openai-codex/... for the OpenAI Codex subscription path instead. Explicit user-supplied openai/... model selections may remain allowed, but they should not be advertised or injected as TLH defaults.

Human decision: TLH code-reviewer should intentionally prefer an available opposite provider for review independence: Anthropic primary sessions should prefer bundled OpenAI Codex review models when available, and OpenAI/OpenAI-Codex primary sessions should prefer bundled Anthropic review models when available. This must be implemented through provider-aware subagent injection, not an authoritative frontmatter model default, so OpenAI API-only users are not forced onto unavailable Codex. Make this behavior explicit in docs.

Human decision on 2026-06-12: TLH-maintained upstream forks should use a PR-first workflow. For fork fixes or bundled extension changes, open a pull request in the fork and wait for review/merge before creating reachable TLH tags, bumping TLH pins, or releasing those changes, unless the user explicitly overrides this flow. This generalizes the existing pi-subagents PR-first rule to TLH forks broadly.

Human decision for issue #136: terminal subagent child runs should clean up OS processes they started. Scope is owned process groups created by the subagent runner on POSIX/macOS; hard terminal states (complete, failed, cancelled, explicit hard stopped) should SIGTERM then SIGKILL after a short grace period, while soft pause/resume remains non-destructive. Do not use global name/cwd process sweeps such as pkill/killall; deliberate daemon escapes like setsid/launchctl are out of phase-1 scope except for warnings.

package-lock.json is now tracked in the repo (started 2026-06-17). It was previously untracked (not gitignored). Decision came from the human while fixing gh-156: dev deps were refreshed from 0.76.0 to @earendil-works/* 0.79.6 to match the runtime Pi version, and the lock file is committed to pin the dependency tree for reproducible installs. Do not delete it assuming it's an accidental artifact.

Human decision from 2026-06-15: delta-scoped follow-up code-reviewer behavior must be opt-in through TLH /experimental machinery, not present in default architect or code-reviewer prompts. The default prompts should continue ordinary/full-diff review behavior unless the experimental feature is enabled.

Human decision from 2026-06-15 supersedes gxqmtq: make the run-tests-last/final-validation-ticket workflow permanent TLH architect behavior instead of an opt-in /experimental feature. Remove the run-tests-last experimental command surface rather than keeping a toggle.

Human correction from 2026-06-15 supersedes part of mduuqn: keep TLH /experimental infrastructure for future feature flags, but remove run-tests-last from the experimental feature list/toggle surface because its workflow is now permanent architect behavior.

TLH suppresses the upstream Pi 'Update Available — Run `pi update`' launch banner with a prototype no-op override of InteractiveMode.prototype.showNewVersionNotification (extensions/the-last-harness/new-version-notice.ts), mirroring the existing package-update-notice.ts override. Reason: TLH pins Pi to a supported version window, so prompting users to 'pi update' is misleading — the correct path is 'tlh update'.

Rejected alternative: setting PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 in the tlh wrapper. That env var ALSO gates TLH's own update notifier (update-check.ts shouldStop), so it would silence the 'The Last Harness update available' notice too; it is additionally a documented user opt-out in docs/install.md. So PI_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK semantics are intentionally left unchanged and the upstream version fetch still runs harmlessly — only the banner render is no-op'd. Do not 'simplify' this to the env var.

Fail-open posture is deliberate: the override skips (console.warn, no throw, does NOT set the Symbol.for guard) if the upstream method is missing/non-function. A canary test (tests/the-last-harness-extension-new-version-notice.test.mjs) asserts the REAL upstream method exists pre-patch so a Pi version bump that renames/removes it fails loudly instead of silently letting the banner reappear. This is separate from the lastChangelogVersion=9999 changelog pin.

TLH installer must NEVER auto-remove or modify anything under ~/.local. The private pinned pi runtime at ~/.the-last-harness/runtime is fully self-contained and the wrapper execs it by absolute path, so an old ~/.local pi is harmless and ignored. REJECTED: guarded auto-cleanup of a legacy ~/.local pi during install/update (even when guarded by ownership + exact pinned version + a 'private runtime absent at start of run' migration heuristic). Reason: once on the private-runtime model, install-state piInstalledByTlh=true means 'TLH owns the private runtime', which is effectively always true and cannot be reliably distinguished from a user-owned ~/.local pi. Every heuristic leaked at least one data-loss edge (notably: a user who deletes the runtime dir then runs tlh update, while owning their own ~/.local/bin/pi@0.79.7, would have it uninstalled). Also REJECTED as over-engineered: adding a durable install-state migration marker to make auto-cleanup safe. Final decision (human-directed): drop installer auto-removal entirely, no hint. Manual cleanup is documented in README/docs only. The uninstaller mirrors this: it removes the private runtime when TLH-owned, but only removes a ~/.local pi under an explicit --force-include-pi flag. If tempted to re-add 'tidy up the old ~/.local pi' automation, don't — it was deliberately removed for safety.

TLH private-runtime ownership is determined by an affirmative marker file <runtime>/.tlh-runtime-owned (schemaVersion 1, packageName, realpath-matched runtimeAbsPath, origin created|migrated), NOT by the directory's shape. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: inferring ownership from the top-level {bin, lib, node-compile-cache} layout or from the presence of lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent. Empirically, a shared npm --prefix (e.g. one also holding 'some-other-tool') matches that shape identically, so shape-based ownership caused install to clobber and 'tlh uninstall' to rm -rf a user's shared prefix (data loss). Verified by repro: unmarked foreign prefix -> install REFUSES; uninstall SKIPS and preserves foreign packages even with --force-include-pi + piInstalledByTlh=true. Do NOT reintroduce shape-based ADOPT of unmarked prefixes; migration of legacy installs is provenance-gated on piInstalledByTlh=true in <agentDir>/tlh/install-state.json, which then writes a marker (origin=migrated). Both install (assertRuntimePrefixOwnedOrEmpty in scripts/tlh-install.mjs) and uninstall.sh fail closed: missing/malformed/symlinked/path-mismatched marker -> never delete.

Human decision: the new contrarian subagent should be shipped behind TLH /experimental rather than enabled by default. Pre-ticket planning is exactly the intended moment for contrarian when a proposed change genuinely warrants adversarial review, but it should use a sparing bar like oracle: meaningful uncertainty, tradeoff, blast radius, hard-to-undo direction, or debatable assumptions, tied to a named opposing case rather than automatic use.

Human decision from 2026-06-25: TLH anonymous launch telemetry should include allowlisted registered experimental feature states as on/off values so adoption can be measured. Send all registered features on each normal launch, including off states; do not send unknown/custom feature strings from settings; respect existing telemetry opt-outs; use string states rather than booleans for TelemetryDeck compatibility.

2026-06-25 startup launch target: TLH should stay below 1000ms steady-state to first TLH header in the interactive TUI. Local measurements in the TLH repo showed normal 'tlh' first-header mean 1081.77ms across 5 runs including a cold first-run outlier, but 988.57ms mean after excluding that outlier; controlled offline runs with update/telemetry skipped showed first-header mean 1024.55ms across 10 runs, 993.43ms excluding the first-run outlier. Treat the practical objective as preserving sub-1000ms steady-state first-header launch time. Biggest observed contributors were base Pi/Node/TUI startup (~430ms), installed package/resource discovery (~250ms), and extension code load/activation (~250-300ms); collectStartupResources/session_start was only ~10-20ms and is not the primary ROI target by itself.

Human decision supersedes xjrnnd: contrarian should now be promoted out of TLH /experimental and enabled by default as a bundled minor subagent. Keep the sparing usage bar and strongest-opposing-case guidance, but no longer require /experimental enable contrarian before delegation.

Human decision: TLH minor subagents should follow the active architect/session provider by default; only code-reviewer, oracle, and contrarian should intentionally prefer an available opposite provider for independence. For GPT/OpenAI defaults, continue using the OpenAI Codex subscription provider path (openai-codex/...) rather than regular openai/... API defaults.

TLH CI monitoring should use long-running polling with an immediate first check, then 30s, 60s, 2m, 5m, 10m, 15m, 20m, 30m, then hourly. User-facing prompts should not list every timing; describe it concisely as a long-running/background CI watch and surface details only if useful or requested.

Human decision for RTK native migration: TLH should force-remove the old bundled pi-rtk package/fork during the migration and should not preserve historical 'rtk' entries in tlh.disabledDefaultExtensions. This release is significant enough to re-enable RTK by default because native RTK should work better. After the migration, user opt-outs created against the new RTK integration must be respected. TLH should always install/manage the rtk binary even when the user disables the extension so re-enabling is immediate.

Human decision for RTK native migration: managed RTK binary installation/validation is required. On supported platforms, if TLH cannot install or validate the pinned managed rtk binary, install/update should fail hard rather than warn and continue.

2026-06-29: User published the TLH pi-intercom fork to npm as npm:@diegopetrucci/pi-intercom@0.6.1 and approved using that scoped npm package for TLH's bundled critical intercom default instead of the git fork pin. Temp-profile timing with Pi 0.80.2 found intercom-only fresh install median improved from 3.454s for git:github.com/diegopetrucci/pi-intercom@tlh-v0.6.0-6 to 1.099s for npm:@diegopetrucci/pi-intercom@0.6.1; direct isolated update improved from 0.798s to 0.337s. Caveats: 3 alternating samples, warm shared temp cache, intercom-only not full installer.

Human decision on 2026-06-29: for TLH-maintained forked extensions that are bundled as defaults, publishing scoped npm packages is the preferred path over pinning git fork refs when the package is ready. The intent is faster, smaller, more registry-native installs while preserving conservative settings migration from existing git/source identities via replaces/migrateReplacements.

Human decision on 2026-06-30: when TLH ships a customized version of a bundled extension, TLH should migrate/replace upstream, manually installed, and older TLH default variants so the isolated profile always uses the TLH-customized package when one exists.

2026-06-30 local offline TLH launch profiling (no npm downloads; temp cloned profile; PI_OFFLINE=1 TLH_SKIP_UPDATE_CHECK=1 TLH_SKIP_TELEMETRY=1): check-startup-performance warm first-header averaged 1396ms over 7 warm runs, then 1355ms over 5 warm runs, with cold first temp-profile runs around 5.0s. PI_TIMING/PI_STARTUP_BENCHMARK warm internal TOTAL for full profile was ~943-1044ms, dominated by createAgentSessionRuntime (~832-939ms) plus interactiveMode.init (~100-106ms); the ~300ms gap to first-header is mostly Node/static import/process startup plus wrapper/PTY overhead. Disabling extensions dropped internal warm TOTAL to ~43ms; TLH package only was ~376-397ms, so bundled default extensions account for most of the remaining launch cost. Leave-one-out and add-one profiling pointed to pi-web-access as the largest contributor (~216ms add-one, ~250ms saving when removed), followed by pi-mcp-adapter and pi-subagents (~100ms scale), with wrapper shell overhead only ~27ms. Treat extension load/activation as the main ROI target rather than wrapper or collectStartupResources.

2026-06-30 extension lazy-loading investigation: Pi's current extension loader imports each extension module and awaits its factory before startup continues; session_start handlers were mostly cheap in local stubs, so deferring session_start work alone is not enough. Fresh-ish per-extension load measurements pointed at TLH main (~307ms), pi-web-access (~247ms), pi-mcp-adapter (~178ms), pi-subagents (~91ms), anthropic-auth (~39ms), intercom (~30ms), and annotate-git-diff (~23ms) as the meaningful startup load costs. A direct ResourceLoader-style probe showed package resolve itself warm around 2-3ms, skills around 1-2ms, prompts near 0ms, and loadExtensions around 500ms warm within the same process. Temporary-profile PI_TIMING showed disabling web-access+mcp dropped internal warm TOTAL from ~904ms to ~556ms; disabling web-access+mcp+subagents dropped it to ~472ms. Best implementation direction is thin startup facades that register command/tool schemas and lazy-import implementations on first command/tool use; use default/simple sync renderers because renderCall/renderResult cannot await dynamic import. Loader-level lazy extension metadata or JS precompilation may help later, but package-level facades are the lowest-risk first path.

Human clarified that Pi authors explicitly warn against parallel extension loading for startup optimization: extension ordering/side-effect semantics are risky, and Node parse/compile work is single-threaded anyway. Treat parallel extension loading as rejected for TLH startup work unless upstream Pi changes the loader contract. Focus optimization on pi-web-access (~247ms load) and pi-mcp-adapter (~178ms load) first.

pi-web-access startup investigation: a temp-profile prototype replacing the extension entrypoint with a thin lazy facade dropped TLH internal warm TOTAL from ~932ms to ~698ms; disabling pi-web-access entirely measured ~675ms, so a facade can recover nearly all of pi-web-access's ~247ms load cost with roughly ~20-25ms residual overhead. Per-module import probes pointed to extract.ts and its video/youtube/Gemini extraction graph as the main load sink; temp stubbing extract saved ~80ms inside the current monolithic index, but stubbing all obvious heavy dependencies still left ~60ms warm due to the 2300-line index itself. Therefore the optimization should not just dynamic-import helpers inside index.ts; it should make package.json point at a tiny facade entrypoint that registers the public tools/commands/shortcuts and lazy-loads the current runtime on first tool/command/shortcut use.

Human clarified on 2026-07-03 that TLH should not auto-switch users between primary agents for the foreseeable future. The intended investigation is TLH workflow evals, not automatic Architect/Rush routing.

Human decision on 2026-07-05: TLH-maintained fork packages bundled by The Last Harness are not intended to be supported as general standalone distribution targets. Their public/package docs should preserve install and usage information where useful, but must position the forked package as TLH-owned distribution plumbing that exists to serve TLH's bundled/pinned isolated-profile workflow unless the user explicitly decides to broaden support later.

Human decision on 2026-07-05: TLH should remove subagent chain workflow support from the diegopetrucci/pi-subagents fork as a deliberate product/safety choice, not treat chain absence as a bug. Rationale: TLH's supervising architect workflow relies on explicit approval, ticketed one-task developer handoffs, and independent review; chains risk hiding multi-step automation and unapproved follow-up edits. Tracking issue: https://github.com/diegopetrucci/pi-subagents/issues/42

This product/safety decision is fulfilled and remains current in the first-party runtime: saved chains and chain dispatch are excluded from TLH's supported model-facing subagent contract. The old fork issue link is provenance only. Any future reconsideration belongs in this repository and must not become a standalone subagent fork pin or release task.

rtk >= 0.35.0 intentionally exits 3 (not 0) from 'rtk rewrite <supported-cmd>' when no explicit allow rule matches, while still printing the rewritten command (upstream rtk-ai/rtk commit 41a6c6b, security hardening; upstream treats this as permanent, still present in v0.43.0). tlh validation in scripts/tlh-rtk.mjs and extensions/rtk.ts accepts exit 0 or 3. Rejected alternative: re-pinning RTK to v0.34.0 (last exit-0 release, 2026-03) to restore exit-0 behavior — too old, weaker permission model; do not retry a downgrade if exit-3 issues resurface, fix the consumer instead.

Issue #302 (port uninstall.sh from bash to a typed .mts/.mjs runtime script, mirroring install.sh -> tlh-install.mts) was DEFERRED by human decision, not done. Reason: uninstall.sh is the product's recovery/destruction path and is deliberately self-contained (no Node, no support-file fetches; header says so) so it works when the managed Node runtime it removes is broken/absent. A port — even a 'self-contained bundled .mjs' variant — reintroduces a hard Node dependency (must exist, be >=22.19.0, start cleanly, be uncontaminated by NODE_OPTIONS/loaders/PATH) on exactly the path that must survive a broken environment; that regression outweighs the maintainability/typed-parser win. Instead we took the narrow alternative: keep uninstall.sh authoritative bash (already shellcheck-covered via #300) and expand test coverage — adversarial marker/state JSON fail-closed cases and special-char path word-splitting cases in scripts/installer-smoke/uninstall-runtime.sh, plus a CI-only Node oracle (tests/uninstall-parser-oracle.test.mjs) that drives real 'uninstall.sh --dry-run' and checks its bash-parser decisions, adding NO runtime Node dependency. Also decided (Option A): the sed-based runtime-marker parser is intentionally lenient value-extraction, NOT JSON-grammar validation; a grammar-only-malformed marker (e.g. trailing comma) whose ownership fields all still match (schemaVersion/packageName/runtimeAbsPath/origin + pi layout) INTENTIONALLY still permits removal, because ownership is proven. Only re-open the full port if concrete Bash-caused uninstall defects appear that cannot be fixed narrowly.

text: Pi 0.81.x removed ModelRegistry.authStorage. As of upstream @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 0.81.0 (bumped into TLH by PR #366), ModelRegistry became a thin synchronous facade over a new ModelRuntime and no longer exposes authStorage (nor authStorage.get()/runtimeOverrides). This silently broke the TLH footer subscription-usage segment for Anthropic AND OpenAI Codex OAuth users: extensions/the-last-harness/subscription-usage.ts resolved every provider as 'ineligible' (authStorage undefined), and because isUsingOAuth() still returned true the dollar-cost fallback stayed suppressed too — so footer line 3 vanished entirely. The port (ts-jxs5) maps to the new API: eligibility via isUsingOAuth(model) + getProviderAuthStatus(provider) where AuthStatus.source==='runtime' now signals a runtime credential override (replaces the old authStorage.runtimeOverrides Map); access token via await getApiKeyForProvider(provider); cache key still the SHA-256 token fingerprint (see xkryrh). Because getApiKeyForProvider is async but the footer display path is sync, refresh() now records the active cache key / eligibility per provider and the sync path reads that. Codex account-id (for the ChatGPT-Account-Id header) is no longer readable from stored credentials, so it is best-effort decoded from the JWT access-token payload claim 'https://api.openai.com/auth'.chatgpt_account_id (no signature check, no network); omitted if absent. The legacy authStorage code path is retained as a fallback for Pi <= 0.80.x, so the entry xkryrh behavior still applies there.

Method: read-only corpus classification of 860 notification deliveries across both TLH profiles + delivery-path map of pinned pi-subagents 0.31.8 (release commit af8c168) and pi-intercom 0.8.0. KEY TIMELINE: both 0.31.7 (native async completions + upstream #489 dispose-on-shutdown) and 0.31.8 pins landed 2026-07-21, the LAST day of the audit window, so #379's headline numbers (578/140/64) are almost entirely PRE-FIX. Also #524 (collapse management output) ABSENT - verbosity not correctness. text:
2026-07-23 root-cause investigation of #378 (acceptance-contract false rejections). Method: read-only classification of 67 acceptance-failure candidates across both TLH profiles (window 2026-06-28..present) + architecture map of pinned pi-subagents tlh-v0.31.9 @ 5917b7a (no acceptance diffs vs deployed 0.31.8). HEADLINE: the acceptance gate produced ZERO true positives — 33 no-edit-guard holds (safety successes miscounted as failures), 18 impossible-'reviewed' false rejections (exact audit match; STILL RECURRING, 4 post-0.31.8), 12 empty-array evidence-shape false rejections, 4 pause/SIGINT runs scored as rejected, 0 genuine failures. ROOT CAUSES (verified in pinned code): (1) inference from agent name+task text+run-shape flags, no role metadata (#466 absent); async/dynamic write runs INFER 'reviewed' which always rejects post-run without an independent reviewResult (#440 preflight absent); (2) explicit acceptance can strengthen but never weaken inferred policy — cannot opt out at dispatch; (3) checked+ modes require non-empty changedFiles/tests/commandsRun (#442 absent) so valid no-change work (read-only investigation tickets run through write-capable developer) cannot comply; (4) pause/interrupt scored as rejection. Evaluation is mechanical (no LLM judge). DESIGN DECISION (architect analysis, human-directed 'ok to deviate from upstream'): in TLH every child run already has an intelligent judge (the architect); independent review is an explicit architect decision; therefore the mechanical gate's only legitimate jobs are integrity verification + structural report completeness — 'reviewed' (auto-spawned second reviewer) is philosophically incompatible with TLH, same reasoning as subagent-chain removal (vseuvc). PLAN: fork P1 never-infer + preflight-reject 'reviewed' (small, kills the only live class); P2 pause-not-rejected; P3 role frontmatter + role-shaped evidence profiles with verified declared-no-changes path, guard-holds as success signals; P4 (deferred) full claimed-vs-actual diff verification — no dishonesty observed to justify it now. Then TLH declares role: on all 8 subagents + prompt alignment + pin bump. Artifacts: .pi-subagents/artifacts/378-acceptance-investigation/ (gitignored).

--- CURRENT TLH SUPERSESSION (2026-08-05) ---
The standalone fork plan and pin-bump tail above are fulfilled and superseded by bdysgr. Its empirical rejection classes and architect-as-judge design rationale remain useful; current acceptance behavior is first-party under extensions/subagents, including dispatch rejection of reviewed, skipped pause/interruption acceptance, and role-shaped evidence. Make any further change and review in TLH, never through a standalone subagent release.

text: During the #94 paused-async-resume acceptance-contract work (fork pi-subagents, PR #99), two independent same-provider (Anthropic) code-reviewer passes both returned APPROVE, but a cross-provider review on OpenAI (openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol) then found two real gaps both had missed: attached-root paused children never persist interrupted (chain-root-attachment.ts computes paused state then drops it), and the fail-closed acceptance guard was bypassable for non-skipped / element-malformed ledgers. text:
On 2026-08-01 the human raised a tweet arguing new projects should instrument distributed tracing from day one, sample everything, and use one telemetry stream instead of analytics providers. We evaluated it and deliberately rejected the remote-tracing mechanism for TLH: TLH is a local CLI running on end users' machines, so 'sample all of them' would mean exfiltrating prompts, cwd, repo names and tool args, which directly contradicts the docs/telemetry.md contract; it would also tax the warm-startup budget the project defends. Remote telemetry stays as-is (one pseudonymous launch event). Do not re-propose OTLP export, a tracing vendor, or session replay unless the human raises it.

What we built instead is local, read-only analysis tooling over data that already exists on disk (scripts/lib/session-analysis.mts and scripts/tlh-sessions.mts).

Two findings worth keeping because they cost real effort to establish. First, an initial analysis wrongly concluded there was no parent/child correlation in session data; the oracle corrected this and it was verified empirically — subagent tool results already carry details.runId and details.results[].sessionFile, so the correlation graph can be built with no instrumentation changes at all. Child sessions nest at <cwd-slug>/<parent-stem>/<runId>/run-N/session.jsonl, so a shallow glob misses all of them and makes the data look absent. Second, pi-subagents run-history.jsonl is foreground-only, so error rates derived from it are not representative of all subagent runs.

Deliberately deferred, in priority order if this is picked up again: adding toolCallId to ChildTranscriptEvent in the pi-subagents fork (gated on the CLI actually demonstrating a pairing gap, and the fork was 190 commits behind upstream); making run-history reads pure and isolating test agents from real history (relates to issue #380); and refactoring tokens-analyzer.ts and session-limit-report-*.ts onto the shared module plus adding a latency column to /tokens, both held back until the module contract is proven by real use.

--- CURRENT TLH SUPERSESSION (2026-08-05) ---
The privacy decision, local-analysis approach, session correlation facts, and run-history limitation above remain current. If a demonstrated pairing gap justifies toolCallId later, evaluate and selectively implement it in first-party extensions/subagents; the old fork-lag context is historical and creates no fork pin/release/sync follow-up. The separate TLH script refactors remain governed by their original evidence threshold.

text:
Follow-up to htnwpp. On 2026-08-01 the deferred '/tokens refactor' was reconsidered and deliberately scoped down. Investigation showed tokens-analyzer.ts and scripts/lib/session-analysis.mts share almost nothing: the former analyses the live in-memory session via sessionManager.getEntries() and is branch-aware through activeLeafId, computing cost/token/cache-miss data with zero toolCallId usage; the latter streams from disk and computes timing and correlation. Refactoring /tokens onto the disk module was rejected as strictly worse — it would have lost branch-awareness, added I/O to an interactive command, and pulled scripts/ code toward the extension path.

What was done instead: extract only the pure pairing function into extensions/the-last-harness/tool-pairing.ts, shared by both, and add a median observed-latency column to /tokens. Refactoring session-limit-report-*.ts onto the shared module was dropped entirely as 1066 lines of risk for no user-visible gain; it serves a different purpose (windowed session-limit accounting) and works.

Non-obvious constraint worth remembering: this required a .mts file under scripts/ importing a generated .js from extensions/. tsconfig.json covers extensions/**/*.ts and scripts/**/*.ts but not scripts/**/*.mts, while tsconfig.runtime-scripts.json covers only scripts/**/*.mts. The import works under NodeNext with allowJs, and both typecheck configs pass, but the direction matters — put shared pure code in the extension tree and import it from scripts, not the reverse, otherwise the extension would depend on scripts/ and risk the startup path.

Also: tests/package-runtime-smoke.test.mjs hardcodes the count of generated extension modules (68 -> 69 here). That is an intentional tripwire, not a bug; do not soften it into a range or dynamic recount. Note it asserts before the Pi version check later in the same test, so a stale count failure masks a version-pin failure and makes it look like the version problem disappeared.

text:
Empirical lesson from PR #415 (2026-08-01), not reconstructable from the code: local 'npm run validate' can silently under-report.

The validate chain is sequential and fails fast: check:package-versions -> typecheck -> typecheck:runtime -> check:runtime -> installer smoke -> npm test -> lint -> lint:sh -> merge-settings dry-run -> npm pack. Because 'npm test' precedes 'lint', a failing test aborts the run before lint executes. In this session a stale local node_modules (Pi 0.81.1 while package.json pinned 0.82.1) failed npm test, so 7 real lint errors were never surfaced locally and only appeared in CI's 'Non-test validation' job, which runs lint independently of tests.

Two consequences worth remembering. First, 'npm run validate passed except known failures' is not a safe claim when a test fails — later stages simply did not run. When tests fail locally, run lint and lint:sh directly before believing the tree is clean. Second, the two failures repeatedly treated as pre-existing in this repo (the Pi version pin and the claude-opus-5 model-catalog absence) were BOTH just stale local dependencies; CI passed all tests on the same commits. Run 'npm ci' before concluding a failure is pre-existing.

Related masking effect inside a single test: tests/package-runtime-smoke.test.mjs asserts a hardcoded generated-extension-module count (line ~89) BEFORE it asserts the Pi runtime version (line ~115). Adding an extension module makes the count assertion fail first and hides the version assertion, which makes the failure appear to change nature between runs. The hardcoded count is a deliberate tripwire and should not be softened into a range or a dynamic recount.

text:
Packaging constraint discovered in PR #415 (2026-08-01) that has no single code anchor: a packaged prompt in prompts/ must never invoke a packaged script by a cwd-relative path.

prompts/ ships in package.json files[], and the installer places the package as a git checkout at <agent-dir>/git/github.com/<owner>/<repo>/. When an end user runs a slash command, cwd is their own project, so 'node scripts/foo.mjs' cannot resolve. The prompt appears to work in the tlh-snake repo and is broken for every real user — a failure mode that repo-local testing cannot catch.

Deriving an absolute path from the install layout inside the prompt was considered and REJECTED: the path embeds owner and repo, and forks genuinely exist (a BeaNuman/the-last-harness checkout was observed locally alongside diegopetrucci/the-last-harness), so a hardcoded layout would break for fork installs.

The accepted pattern is to expose the script as an installer-owned wrapper subcommand in scripts/tlh-wrapper.mts, following defaults/tickets/doctor: a tlh_package_<name>_script_is_usable guard that tells the user to run 'tlh update' when files are missing, plus a block that execs from . Pass --agent-dir "" explicitly rather than relying on the exported PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, per the repo's explicit-paths guideline; user-supplied flags still override because the CLI is last-wins.

Testing gotcha for this pattern: a temp install clones the default branch, so a newly added script is absent and the guard correctly refuses. That is not a bug. To prove the subcommand end to end, copy the new script and its transitive imports into the checkout at default_tlh_package_root, and separately confirm 'npm pack' ships them.

When an extension sends a prompt via pi.sendUserMessage, deliverAs must be supplied or feedback can be silently lost. ExtensionAPI.sendUserMessage forwards deliverAs as streamingBehavior into AgentSession.prompt(); if the agent is streaming and streamingBehavior is absent, prompt() throws 'Agent is already processing...' and the runtime wrapper swallows that rejection into an extension error the user never sees. deliverAs is ignored when the agent is idle, so 'followUp' is safe unconditionally.

/annotate-last-message and /annotate-git-diff both pass deliverAs: 'followUp' for this reason, and their tests assert on it.

extensions/the-last-harness/review.ts still calls pi.sendUserMessage(envelope) with no deliverAs. This is a known latent bug, not an oversight: it was found while adding auto-send to the two annotate commands and deliberately left out of scope to keep that change reviewable. /review is normally invoked when the agent is idle, which is why it has not bitten yet. Recording it because the fix was never written, so there is no code to comment on.

Packaged agent thinking levels are declared explicitly per provider — tlhAnthropicThinking and tlhOpenaiThinking on all 12 agents — and the shared base 'thinking:' frontmatter field was deliberately removed. Explicitness was chosen over DRY at the human's direction: repeating the same level in both fields (10 of 12 agents are high/high) is intended, not an oversight. Do not 'simplify' this by reintroducing a single shared thinking field. The base field is retained only in the TypeScript type and frontmatter parser as a compatibility fallback for user-authored and pi-native agents, not for packaged ones.

Removing the base field from packaged agents was load-bearing, not cosmetic. TLH injects the resolved level as a ':level' suffix on the model string, and pi-subagents re-applies frontmatter thinking on top of that suffix, producing a double suffix if both were present.

Also learned empirically: TLH's older tlhOpenaiThinking field never did anything. It was written onto the subagent tool input, but pi-subagents declares that tool schema with additionalProperties:false, does not declare 'thinking', and never reads it. Frontmatter and the model-string suffix are the only channels it honours.

RESOLVED: 'max' is a valid Pi thinking level. Verified against the live runtime pi-coding-agent@0.83.0 / pi-ai@0.83.0, where ThinkingLevel is minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max, and pi's CHANGELOG documents max as an opt-in level above xhigh natively supported on GPT-5.6 and adaptive Claude models. Per-model catalog confirms gpt-5.6-luna supports low,medium,high,xhigh,max and claude-sonnet-4-6 has thinkingLevelMap {max:max} with low/medium/high supported implicitly (absent map entries are allowed; only explicit nulls and the xhigh/max opt-in gate exclude a level). So developer at medium on Anthropic and max on OpenAI are both valid.

Beware stale evidence when re-checking this: several nested copies of pi-ai on disk (0.74.2, 0.75.5) predate max and will suggest it does not exist. The authoritative copy is the one bundled under the active runtime dir, not the agent/npm node_modules tree, and not the pi-coding-agent devDependency pinned in package.json.

The fork side of this is fixed in diegopetrucci/pi-subagents#123, which adopts upstream 747de756: pi-subagents had TWO stale THINKING_LEVELS copies omitting max — src/shared/model-info.ts (drove a status-badge mis-render) and a local duplicate in src/runs/shared/pi-args.ts (drove the double suffix) — and the duplicate is now removed in favour of importing the shared list. A code comment describing the gap was briefly present at the injection site in extensions/the-last-harness/model-defaults.ts and was deliberately removed once the fork fix existed, because it would have become misleading as soon as TLH's pin moved. The fix does not reach TLH until PR #123 merges, the fork is released, and TLH's @diegopetrucci/pi-subagents pin in config/default-extensions.json moves off 0.31.11.

text:
npm run check:startup-performance can fail with a misleading extension-load crash on machines that have more than one TLH profile installed.

defaultProfileSource() in scripts/check-startup-performance.mjs prefers $PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR and clones that profile's agent dir into a temp workspace, but createTemporaryWrapper() takes piCmd from whatever 'tlh' resolves to on PATH. If those two belong to different installs, the checker launches one profile's agent dir under another profile's Pi binary. A Pi version mismatch there surfaces as:

  Failed to load extension '.../extensions/the-last-harness.js': Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prototype')

which looks like a TLH bug or a Node incompatibility but is neither. Observed during v0.33.0 release prep: PATH 'tlh' pointed at ~/.tlh-numan (a BeaNuman fork, Pi 0.80.6) while PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR was ~/.the-last-harness-main (Pi 0.83.0, the repo-pinned version). No mean was produced at all.

Workaround: pass a wrapper whose baked-in default_pi_cmd matches the profile being measured, e.g.
  node scripts/check-startup-performance.mjs --command ~/.local/bin/tlh-main --profile-source ~/.the-last-harness-main/agent
That produced a warm first-header mean of 673ms against the 1000ms release budget.

Canonical single-profile installs cannot hit this: PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is unset, so the checker falls through to ~/.the-last-harness/agent, which is the same default_agent_dir baked into that install's own wrapper. Diagnose by comparing 'grep default_pi_cmd $(which tlh)' against $PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR before assuming a real regression.

text:
The TLH telemetry work was deliberately split into two PRs: effective-configuration reporting landed first (#408, merged 58665c9), and per-session activity metrics (Tlh.Session.primaryTurns/.cacheMisses/.agentRuns) was deferred.

The split was not about PR size. Configuration reporting reads state that already exists in memory or in settings files, so it is safe by construction. The metrics half has to durably track which session files it has already counted across process restarts, and that watermark machinery kept producing adjacent bugs: each review round fixed one and surfaced another (equal-mtime cursor permanently skipping sessions, install-id state truncation, failed sends recorded as delivered, parentId ancestry broken by malformed-entry filtering). Landing config reporting unblocked the useful half rather than holding it behind a durability redesign.

Rejected along the way: emitting a session_shutdown event to report metrics at session end. It does not fire on uncaught exception, dead terminal, or SIGKILL, so it would bias the data toward clean exits. Also rejected: inter-process file locking for the watermark, as disproportionate for best-effort telemetry (temp+rename is sufficient).

The deferred half is preserved outside the repo at ~/tlh-deferred-session-metrics/ (module, 1550-line test suite, full pre-split patch, reproduced review findings) because deleting it would have lost working code that only needs a durability redesign, not a rewrite.

Actual failure mechanism for the hollow dot while the architect works: (1) TLH's activity-reporters.ts gates rootSession on ctx.hasUI, but pi-subagents children run 'pi --mode json -p' and report hasUI=true, so every child session_shutdown sends pane.release_agent, clearing the pane's hook authority mid-session (705+ releases logged); (2) after a clear, TLH only re-reports on the next activity EDGE (no heartbeat), so long working stretches fall back to screen scraping, which often shows idle on TLH panes; (3) herdr can also clear hook authority server-side when the detected foreground agent flips (state.rs ~516) or on process exit, and e608a751 (v0.8.0, 'fix: make known-agent exit process-owned') added a guard (state.rs:611) dropping non-authority reports while recent_agent_process_exit matches — rare but real. Herdr fixed the same two bugs in its own Pi integration: #2159/5eab32da gates on ctx.mode==='tui' (v8), and e608a751 removed pane.release_agent entirely (v7). Fix plan, all on TLH side, no upstream needed: (a) gate rootSession on ctx.mode==='tui'; (b) stop sending pane.release_agent (ownership via process exit); (c) add a periodic re-report heartbeat (~15-30s, fresh seq) so any server-side authority clear self-heals; (d) optional: strip HERDR_* env from pi-subagents child spawn env. Foot-guns: seq scheme is Date.now()*1000+counter — never send larger-scale seqs (a stored higher seq permanently blocks the source per terminal until herdr restart); full_lifecycle_hook_authority (hardcoded whitelist in src/detect/mod.rs: pi/omp/mastracode/opencode/kilo/kimi) is still never granted to herdr:tlh, so screen detection keeps running underneath — harmless while hook authority is present. Reproduction/testing trick: isolated scratch server via 'herdr --session <name>' (own socket under ~/.config/herdr/sessions/<name>/) with HERDR_* env stripped, fake pi process via zsh 'exec -a pi node -e ...' (detection matches name=node argv0=pi).

text:
ESLint replaced by Biome 2.5.7 for JS/TS linting and formatting. Decision was human-driven: the repo had no formatter at all, and the human asked whether one tool could also replace ESLint. An audit showed Biome covers 91% of the existing rule surface (83 of 91 rules), collapses four devDependencies (eslint, @eslint/js, typescript-eslint, globals) into one, and the full lint surface checks in roughly 200-300 ms. Migration cost was acceptable.

Accepted tradeoffs: nine ESLint rules are no longer enforced, split into two categories.

Seven have no Biome equivalent. The two meaningful ones are no-invalid-regexp (catches syntactically invalid regex literals) and no-useless-assignment (catches variables assigned but never read after assignment); the other five are low-signal or stylistic.

Two were deliberately left disabled because Biome's counterparts are semantically broader than the ESLint rules they replace: suspicious/noEmptyBlockStatements is not enabled, so no-empty is no longer enforced (Biome's version also flags empty function bodies, which ESLint's does not - 350 hits in the codebase); suspicious/noAssignInExpressions is not enabled, so no-cond-assign is no longer enforced (Biome's version flags all assignments in expressions, not just those in conditions).

Two rules were reclaimed rather than accepted as losses. suspicious/noPrototypeBuiltins is enabled after migrating 25 call sites to Object.hasOwn(). suspicious/noUnusedExpressions is enabled, recovering @typescript-eslint/no-unused-expressions: 'biome migrate' had silently set it to "off" and it was nearly documented as an unavoidable gap. Biome's base rule lacks the TS-variant options allowShortCircuit and allowTernary, which is why migrate declined to map it, but the codebase has zero real violations so nothing is lost in practice.

Operational lesson: 'biome migrate' output must be audited rule by rule. It silently dropped noUnusedFunctionParameters (so unused parameters went unchecked), silently disabled noUnusedExpressions, and emitted an inspired-only rule (useErrorCause) that was never part of the ESLint config. Every "off" entry in biome.json was subsequently audited; the remaining 24 are legitimate (18 base JS rules that typescript-eslint disables in TS context because the compiler catches them, 5 intentional per-path test-file disables, and organizeImports as a documented non-goal).

Formatter config: lineWidth 120, indentStyle tab, quoteStyle double. npm run lint is now biome check scripts tests extensions (non-mutating; fails on unformatted code). 186 tsc-generated files are excluded from formatting via biome.json overrides; npm run check:runtime is the guard for generated-file freshness.

Relates to vjmzsx: that entry records that TypeScript upgrades were gated on typescript-eslint support. With ESLint removed, the typescript-eslint gate no longer applies. Whether Biome's TypeScript parser cadence acts as an equivalent gate was never verified. A future TypeScript upgrade should check Biome's changelog for parser support before assuming the constraint has simply lifted.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
Seven tests in the root suite (as of the Biome migration, ~2026-08-08) assert on SOURCE CODE TEXT — they read source files and regex-match expected strings. The Biome formatter reflows code and broke all seven when formatting was first applied. Any future formatter or formatter-config change will break this class of test again.

These tests are deliberately brittle by design (they verify specific generated output shapes), but the breakage mode is non-obvious: test failures appear as formatting mismatches rather than logic errors. Future contributors should know that 'npm run lint' changes or biome.json config tweaks may require updating these seven assertions even when no logic changed.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
Import sorting (Biome assist/source/organizeImports) is intentionally NOT enforced in the Biome config — it was not enforced under ESLint either. Enabling it would reorder imports in 113 tsc-generated mirror files (same-layout .js/.mjs under scripts/ and extensions/), which permanently conflicts with npm run check:runtime (which verifies generated files are fresh without mutating the worktree).

Adopting import sorting later is a separate change that would require excluding generated files from Biome assist before enabling the rule. Do not switch organizeImports on without that exclusion — it will trigger approximately 300 violations plus generated-output churn on every check:runtime run.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
biome.json is parsed as STRICT JSON and rejects // comments. Adding them silently breaks the entire Biome configuration.

The failure mode is the dangerous part. When biome.json is discovered in the working directory (the normal case, e.g. via 'npm run lint'), Biome SWALLOWS the config parse error and falls back to its DEFAULT recommended ruleset instead of failing loudly. The command still appears to run and still reports a file count. Only when the same config is passed explicitly via --config-path does Biome surface the real diagnostics ("End of file expected", "Incorrect type, expected an object, but received an array").

Symptoms that the config silently stopped loading: violations appear for rules the config never enables (noTemplateCurlyInString, useOptionalChain, noImplicitAnyLet, noUselessContinue), and formatter.lineWidth reverts from 120 to the 80 default, so hundreds of previously-clean files suddenly want reflowing. If a formatting-only change wants to touch hundreds of files, suspect config loading before believing the diff.

This was introduced while trying to document why import sorting is disabled, and it turned 'npm run validate' from exit 0 to exit 1 without any obvious configuration error.

Guard: tests/biome-config.test.mjs asserts biome.json parses under strict JSON.parse and that formatter.lineWidth is 120. Verified to fail if a comment is introduced. Do not weaken or delete this test. If comments in the config are ever genuinely wanted, the correct move is renaming to biome.jsonc, not loosening the guard.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: E′ nudge workaround (issues #468/#470): notification call sites send custom messages without triggerTurn plus a '[tlh]' user nudge, because upstream Pi skips before_agent_start on extension-triggered turns, dropping the TLH system prompt (correctness loss + full prompt-cache invalidation). Human decisions: (1) accepted synthetic user-role nudge messages over losing async wake-up (the fail-closed triggerTurn:false alternative was rejected); (2) the human is filing the upstream Pi issue personally — agents should not file it; (3) remove the workaround per #470 once upstream fixes it and the Pi pin is bumped. Precedent for the upstream report: earendil-works/pi#6162 fixed the sibling bug (tool changes dropping before_agent_start overrides).
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
Never run 'npx biome' in this repo — it silently resolves an UNRELATED npm registry package named 'biome' (version 0.3.3) instead of the repo's @biomejs/biome 2.5.7, and exits 0 without checking anything.

Observed empirically 2026-08-09: with node_modules absent or @biomejs/biome not installed, 'npx biome check scripts tests extensions' printed no output and returned exit 0, producing a false 'lint passes' signal. This fooled both a developer subagent and the orchestrating agent in the same session; the real 'npm run lint' then reported 7 errors.

Always use 'npm run lint' or ./node_modules/.bin/biome directly, and sanity-check the version with './node_modules/.bin/biome --version' (must print 2.5.7). A bare 'biome: command not found' from npm run lint means dependencies are not installed — that is the honest failure, whereas npx masks it.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
A second class of brittle assertion (distinct from the source-text tests in cqjqkj): hardcoded AGGREGATE FILE COUNTS. Two tests assert exact counts of TypeScript sources under extensions/:

  tests/runtime-typescript-infra.test.mjs  — count of extensions/subagents/src/**/*.ts
  tests/package-runtime-smoke.test.mjs     — that count plus non-subagents extension sources

Adding or deleting ANY .ts file under extensions/ breaks them, and the failure message ('97 !== 96') gives no hint about which file changed or that a counter needs bumping.

This already shipped broken: commit fb9e3fb (#471, 'Wake idle parent via user nudge') added extensions/subagents/src/runs/shared/nudge-texts.ts without bumping the counters, leaving main red across several CI runs until it was noticed on 2026-08-09 while investigating CI speed.

Suggested durable fix (recommended in review, not implemented): compare derived source/generated-file SETS rather than totals, so a mismatch names the offending file and no manual counter update is needed.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
Async completion notices are the architect's ENTIRE view of a finished subagent run: pi.sendMessage with role custom is rewritten by upstream convertToLlm into a role user message using content verbatim, while details is dropped and is TUI-only. In 2026-08 the per-child summary cap was raised 1200 -> 8000 and the message ceiling 8000 -> 32000.

Empirical basis, recorded because the source data is perishable local session state and cannot be reconstructed from the codebase. Across 757 local session files there were 169 subagent-notify messages, 86 truncated, and in 86/86 the binding cap was the per-summary cap — the 8000 envelope was never once hit. Across 158 real subagent output artifacts on disk (p50 1772, p75 3064, p90 6267, p95 7556, max 16672), a 1200 cap delivers 35 percent of results complete inline and 8000 delivers 96 percent; the curve knees hard at 8000 (12000 gives 98 percent). Roughly half of truncated notices were followed by the architect reading the advertised artifact path, median 1 entry later — so truncation did not save context, it deferred the same tokens and added a tool round trip.

REJECTED: a shared summary pool divided across children (pool 6000 / n). The human rejected it because a child's report should not shrink purely because it has siblings — each child's result is an independent unit of information. It also regressed against the status quo at n>=6 (750 per child versus the old flat 1200). Budget per child, not per group.

REJECTED: reverting the 32000 ceiling to 8000 on injection-surface grounds. This was formally recommended in code review and declined. Truncating the notification provides little injection protection because the identical child-authored text reaches the architect anyway through an unbounded artifact file read; the cap changes the delivery path, not the exposure. What the ceiling genuinely bounds is context consumption, and that tradeoff was made deliberately with the coverage data above. Note the counter-argument that was conceded: a foreground tool result (200 KB via DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT) is solicited by the model whereas an injected user-role message is not, so the two are not equivalent trust contexts and 'foreground allows more' is not on its own a sufficient justification.

INVARIANT worth protecting: truncation must always preserve the trailing artifact and session reference lines. formatSingleCompletion emits the session line last and the send-time cap cuts from the end, so a naive overflow destroys exactly the recovery pointer the architect needs, converting 'truncated but recoverable' into 'truncated and unrecoverable'. This is enforced across fitPreviewWithinCeiling, joinedLineCost, the batch-entry bound and the send-time cap — four sites with no single home. It was broken twice during implementation by people actively trying to protect it: once by dividing the full envelope across children, once by under-reserving newline separators between batched entries (overshoot of only +2 to +32 chars, which was enough to destroy the last pointer).
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Reviewers twice proposed making /reconcile Reset force model application onto the active session even when the user has set tlh.primaryAgent.applyModel = false. If this behaviour is ever judged wrong, fix it for both commands together, as a deliberate product decision.

text:

text:
When speeding up CI (2026-08-12), the biggest available lever was dropping macos-latest from pull-request runs and keeping it only on main: macOS runners are the critical path (highest wall clock AND highest variance of the six CI jobs) and bill at roughly 10x Linux. Diego explicitly REJECTED this and chose to keep macOS on every PR, accepting the slower/pricier PR path in exchange for catching macOS-specific breakage before merge. Do not re-propose macOS-on-main-only as a CI speedup without new information; the tradeoff was considered and declined deliberately.

Accepted instead: node_modules caching, plus running the previously-sequential commands inside the tests and validation steps as concurrent lanes (scripts/run-lane.mjs). Also considered and dropped as not worth it: raising the test shard count from 2 to 3 (diminishing returns once the step itself is parallelized, and it costs 2 extra runners per run), and merging typecheck:runtime with check:runtime (parallel lanes make the merge pointless while adding semantic risk).

Measured baseline before this work, for future comparison: ~3m20s median wall clock; per test shard the sequential step was ~96s (main tests ~33s, subagents unit ~11s, integration ~49s, e2e ~3s); the validation step was ~53s on ubuntu and ~75s on macOS.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
On 2026-08-13 the human directed that TLH launch telemetry report model and thinking/effort as ONE combined TelemetryDeck dimension instead of two, so the dashboard shows the effective configuration as a single value (e.g. claude-opus-4-5:high) rather than forcing cross-dimension joins. This removed Tlh.Runtime.thinking and the eight Tlh.Subagent.<name>.thinking dimensions.

Two choices were explicit and should not be quietly reverted:
- The separator is a colon because that is what upstream Pi already uses for model+thinking (applyThinkingSuffix, e.g. openai/gpt-5:max). The human's first sketch used a dash; they chose upstream's convention when told about it.
- The keys were RENAMED (Tlh.Runtime.model -> Tlh.Runtime.modelEffort, Tlh.Subagent.<name>.model -> Tlh.Subagent.<name>.modelEffort) specifically so the TelemetryDeck series stays clean: keeping the old key names would have mixed pre-release bare model values with post-release combined values in the same dimension's history. Do not 'simplify' these back to .model.

Effort was also confirmed as the user-facing term for thinking level in telemetry naming, matching the existing /effort command.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
The async lifecycle reservation-erasure flake PREDATED the parallel CI lanes; the lanes only amplified it. This matters because CI on main went red on four consecutive runs immediately after the lanes landed (10897e6, 08-13), which naturally suggests the lanes broke CI and should be reverted. The measured history says otherwise.

Measured from main CI runs (GitHub retains logs ~90 days, so this will not be reconstructable later):
- Before the lanes (08-10 to 08-13, 20 runs): 4 failures, ~20%. Every one was the same flake, always on ubuntu shard 2/2.
- After the lanes, before the fix (4 runs): 4 failures, 100%, now spread across all four platform/shard combinations.
- After the fix (#503, merged as e3dd6ea): green.

Identical signature in all pre-lane failures: 'Timed out waiting for file: .../async-subagent-results/<id>.json' in the 'intercom result delivery cutover' suite, on the 'resume action revives ... paused' tests. Oldest confirmed instance 963e4f0 on 08-10, four days before the lanes.

So the lanes were a better reproducer, not a cause: more concurrency per runner widened the race window and turned a 20% intermittent into a near-deterministic failure. Do not read a post-lanes red streak as evidence against the lane layout without checking the failing test names first.

A related trap: an earlier attempt (342d68e, 'Fix ... CI timeout flake') tried to fix this by scaling timeouts. It could never work, because the failing path writes no result artifact at all, so no wait budget is long enough. Issue #504 tracks making that path fail fast instead of hanging.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
Preference expressed by the maintainer for CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entries: keep them terse, consolidated, and user-facing. Describe the SYMPTOM a user would have noticed, not the internal mechanism — no file paths, function names, ticket ids, or issue numbers. One line is usually right, even when the underlying change was large.

Worked example: a four-commit fix spanning a lifecycle serialization race, timeout scaling, and terminal-state adoption was summarised as the single line 'Fixed async subagent runs that could hang after being paused and resumed.'

Also note that not every merged fix warrants an entry. For the JSONL artifact-flush fix (PR #495) the maintainer explicitly chose NO changelog entry. When a fix is invisible to users or only affects internal test/CI reliability, ask rather than assuming an entry is owed.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
Human decision (2026-08-15) on the 'Context at launch:' header line: it measures context consumed AT LAUNCH ONLY, and that snapshot is deliberately never recomputed.

The allocation is captured once inside scheduleDeferredStartupTask in extensions/the-last-harness.ts and rendered by header.ts. MCP servers that connect lazily mid-session therefore never appear in the line, and its conditional MCP segment stays hidden. This was raised explicitly as a possible defect and the human confirmed it is correct: a server connected later genuinely cost nothing at launch, so omitting it is accurate rather than misleading. The footer's live MCP percentage and /tokens already cover in-session cost.

Do not 'fix' this by adding a recompute or refresh of the launch allocation. Besides being semantically wrong, it would fight the startup budget recorded in entry cyrvbr (<1000ms to first TLH header). There is no code to attach this comment to, because the recompute was deliberately never written.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text:
Installer default output is deliberately compact for ALL installations, not just the main track. The human asked for this explicitly after finding the default install chatty.

Policy: default (non-verbose) installer output shows short progress lines only ('Refreshing installer...', 'Pinning local Pi runtime to <ver>...', 'Installing package...', 'Installing bundled default extensions...'), and closes with 'Done. The Last Harness is ready. Start with:' + blank line + the command wrapped in literal backticks on its own line.

Detail is DEMOTED to --verbose, never deleted: raw stage-0 URL, private-runtime prefix path, '(per-user, no sudo)', bundled-extension count, and the 'The Last Harness installer' header all still print under --verbose. If you need to add installer output, default to verboseLog/verbose_log and only promote to log() if a normal user must act on it.

Explicitly EXCLUDED and re-litigated once already: dry_run_without_stage1() in install.sh keeps the old 'Start with: <cmd>' format. It is a bootstrap/no-stage1 diagnostic approximation with no 'Start with:' label line of its own, so the backtick form leaves a dangling unlabeled command. An attempt to align it was made and deliberately reverted. Do not 'fix' it for consistency.

The PATH-missing warning is emitted BEFORE the summary block (chosen over after-the-command) so the three-line block stays intact and remains the closing statement. It still goes to stderr.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: Notification suppression for in-flight background subagents must never use a wall-clock cap, elapsed-time bound, or activity-gap heuristic. This was explicitly ruled out by the human: async subagents legitimately run for hours, so any time cap fires mid-run and reintroduces the premature 'ready for input' ping the feature exists to eliminate. Prior evidence: an activity-gap watchdog false-fired at 60s while a child was mid tool-execution (.pi-subagents/artifacts/379-notifications-investigation/root-cause-report.md), and pi-subagents' own reconciler uses a 24h threshold for live pids. Suppression is therefore liveness-based only: a job keeps suppressing while there is positive evidence of a live run (a valid pid that responds to signal 0), and anything unverifiable stops counting as active, so the failure mode is an occasional spurious ping rather than a permanently silent session. The 5s periodic check in the tracker is NOT a cap on suppression - it merely re-runs the same pid liveness check, and a healthy long-running child stays suppressed indefinitely. Do not 'simplify' this by adding a maximum suppression duration.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>

text: The notify background-activity gate was shipped fully inert once and every test passed, because the tests pre-created the async run's status.json. In production the parent emits subagent:async-started immediately after spawn and the CHILD writes status.json a moment later, so the tracker's drain read a missing file, concluded the run was gone, and deleted the record permanently. Nothing restored it when the file appeared. When testing anything that consumes async subagent run state, reproduce the real producer ordering - asyncDir present, status.json absent, pid supplied on the event - rather than constructing a fully-formed run directory, or the test will validate a state that never occurs at the moment the code actually runs.
author: Diego Petrucci <baulei@icloud.com>
